messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: Incident #7893 -> HIGH error rate for OrionFin private deployment (vpc-0a1b2c3d). Affects inference endpoints behind NLB. Severity: P1. Paging oncall.
oncall-bot: @sana you are up — acknowledged. Please confirm customer impact and start triage. :rotating_light:
sana: Acknowledged. Seeing ~40% 5xxs from Redwood side to customer NLB. Trying describe-target-health.
sana: aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:acct:targetgroup/tg-orion-1/abcd1234 -> many targets Unhealthy (reason: failed health checks)
sana: Quick check: customer says no infra changes on their side in last hour. OrionFin support pinged. @orion-support can you confirm any recent SG/route/NAT changes?
orion-support: We pushed a security group tweak earlier to restrict inbound to only company IPs, but that was only for web-tier ALB. Nothing touching NLB or backend. We do see some connection resets from our side to Redwood IPs at ~14:05 UTC.
sana: Copy. From our side logs: connections to 10.x.x.x:443 are getting RST or TIME_WAIT, and health checks fail with ECONNRESET. Could be asymmetric routing or wrong return path. Checking route tables + nat gateways now.
sana: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d -> route table rtb-0b2c3d4e points to local for private subnet, NAT gateway nat-05f6e7 present in public subnet.
sana: Checking conntrack on host nodes (we have dedicated pool). ssh into inference-host-11 -> sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.3.
sana: Seeing large conntrack entries for 10.0.3.0/24 -> NAT port exhaustion suspected. Active conntrack count near 65k on node.
maria-netops: That will cause new flows to be dropped. OrionFin uses long-lived websocket-ish connections for streaming; conntrack buildup is expected if ephemeral ports not cleaned. Who modified NAT earlier?
sana: No recent NAT change on Redwood. Could be customer backend returning traffic via a different NAT causing conntrack asymmetry. Also seeing DNS TTLs very low; possible frequent re-resolution amplifying connections.
james: Quick mitigation idea: (1) Add ephemeral port allow rule on customer SG to permit 1024-65535 for TCP established? Wait SGs are stateful, but if return path uses a different egress IP, NAT can break. (2) Temporarily put a small proxy on our side to terminate and reuse connections to reduce conntrack churn. Which is faster?
maria-netops: Proxy deploy might take 10-15 mins. Customer-side SG tweak might be fastest if they agree to relax outbound nat constraints. @orion-support can you temporarily allow outbound to 20.110.0.0/16 (our egress pool) and return ports 1024-65535?
orion-support: We can open outbound to 20.110.0.0/16 for 30 minutes for testing. Applying now.
sana: Thanks. While that propagates, let's restart health checks for the NLB target group to force re-registration: aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn tg-orion-1 --health-check-interval-seconds 10 --health-check-timeout-seconds 4
sana: After forcing recheck, targets still showing initial -> unhealthy. Running tcpdump on node shows SYN from us, no SYN-ACK back.
eng-sre: Can you share the iptables/nat translation table? Also check if there are asymmetric route entries on customer IGW/NAT.
sana: Copied nat table: public NAT gw nat-05f6e7 has high SNAT translations. When customer opened outbound rule we saw immediate decrease in conntrack growth. Health checks starting to succeed for 2/3 targets.
sana: Monitoring token-level errors for the endpoint: 5xxs dropping from 40% -> 6% over 6 minutes.
james: Nice. We'll keep the customer opened rule for 20 more minutes. Meanwhile, schedule a short-lived connection pooler on our side for persistent connections — eng-sre, can you spin up a canary proxy (haproxy) in front of the targets in the dedicated pool? Use host-11, 12. Simple config:
```
frontend fe_stream
  bind :443
  default_backend be_orion
backend be_orion
  server orion1 10.0.3.11:443 check
  server orion2 10.0.3.12:443 check
  option httpchk GET /_health
```

eng-sre: Spinning canary proxy now. Will route a small % via the proxy and keep rest direct.
sana: Customer confirmed their NAT/IGW logs show return traffic successfully hitting 20.110.0.0/16. Health checks now 3/3 healthy at 14:26 UTC. Rolling error rate down to baseline.
orion-support: We rolled back the outbound rule after confirming stability; please confirm we can close or if you need us to keep open for longer.
maria-netops: Let's keep it open for 15 more minutes while we finish cleanup and capture metrics. Also we should capture conntrack delta and nat metrics.
sana: Taking notes for handoff: root cause likely asymmetric egress/NAT causing healthcheck failures and conntrack exhaustion on Redwood hosts because customer return path used a different egress IP range (their change to web-tier SG earlier forced a different NAT path). Mitigation was temporary SG relaxation + forced health check + canary proxy deploy.
sana: Current status: endpoints healthy, error rate <1%, conntrack count falling to normal, no token queue backlog.
james: I'll take the next shift. Handoff summary: incident #7893, impacted OrionFin private deployment vpc-0a1b2c3d, period 14:03-14:30 UTC, customer-facing mitigation coordinated with Orion (SG temporarily opened), infra mitigation: forced target rechecks + canary haproxy proxy to reduce conntrack churn. Next actions: create postmortem, recommend customer config: ensure symmetric egress or static NAT egress IPs; add runbook step for conntrack alerts; consider automating canary proxy deploy for similar cases.
james: @orion-support please send a short customer-facing note we can include in the postmortem about the outbound rule change and any internal reasons for alternate egress.
orion-support: Will provide a blurb in 30m. Also we will consider assigning static NAT IPs for Redwood traffic.
eng-sre: Captured logs and metrics to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/7893/logs.tar.gz. Saved tcpdumps and conntrack dumps.
maria-netops: Postmortem owner: @james. Action items: (1) runbook update for NLB health + conntrack (owner: eng-sre), (2) alert tuning for conntrack > 60k (owner: eng-sre), (3) customer onboarding checklist item to validate symmetric egress or NAT IPs (owner: customer-success).
sana: Closing monitoring window in 20 minutes. If no regression, will mark incident resolved. Thanks all for quick coord. :white_check_mark:
james: Taking over oncall notes and will run the postmortem template. Closing handoff now. :wave:
oncall-bot: Incident #7893 updated: status -> monitoring. Assigned -> james.
pagerduty-bot: Incident #7893 acknowledged by james.
sana: Final check: endpoints healthy for 20 minutes, conntrack stabilized. Looks solved.
james: Marking incident resolved after monitoring window. Will attach customer blurb and timeline to the postmortem.
orion-support: Thanks Redwood team for the quick response. We'll follow up with permanent NAT plan.
sana: Great. Incident closed.
